```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>",
  fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.6, dpi = 110,
  warning = FALSE

```

The discard **raising** side of the package, end to end, for the scheme
actually in use: the **manual grouping**, where the groups of strata that are
raised together - and the data each group's discard rate is estimated from -
are written out by hand. It is a walkthrough, not a test: nothing here asserts
pass or fail, and it is the script to run chunk by chunk in RStudio.

This is vignette **2a** of four. **2b** does the same with groups defined
by the hierarchical cascade, and **3** compares the two, and other, schemes
against each other. This one stays about producing the real deliverable, not
about exploring alternatives to it.

It is driven directly with the vendored RDBESStockCoord functions -
`check_group_conditions()` and `catchRaising()` - the same pattern ICES's own
discard-raising scripts use: a named list of quosures per method
(`strataCond` = which strata a group claims, `matchedDataCond` = which data its
discard rate is estimated from), checked, then raised. Nothing wraps that
call.

The last two sections build the two output data sets this whole vignette
exists for:

* **CC** (Catch Combined) - one row per `catchCategory`, the stock-wide raised
  total;
* **CAR / CAS** - every raised row, and the donor strata behind each group's
  rate,

following the schema of a real ICES stock-annex CAR / CAS export. They are
built inline, as plain data frames, on purpose - not wrapped in functions and
not written to csv yet. Once the shape is right, both become functions that
build and save these data sets; that is future work.

# Data

Brill, `bll.27.3a47de`, 2025, from the CEF csv file under
`inst/extdata/data_CEF_format` (local to this machine; the file is not in the
repository). Only the catch table is needed for raising.

```{r load, message = FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(rcef)

cef_dir <- file.path("..", "inst", "extdata", "data_CEF_format")

# blank cells (no discard domain, no trip count ...) read as NA
catch_data <- read.csv(file.path(cef_dir, "bll", "bll_2025_catches_CEF_v17.1.csv"),
                       na.strings = "")
```

`derive_fields()` is what turns raw CEF into strata-ready data: it parses
`metier4` (and `target`, `mesh`) out of `fleetValue` and the ICES area
levels out of `areaValue`, plus `Country` and `Season`.

```{r derive}
catch_data <- derive_fields(x = catch_data)
nrow(catch_data)
```

There is no `build_strata()` or `add_stratum_metrics()` call here: the manual
scheme's conditions are plain `metier4` / `catchCategory` / `fleetValue` tests
against `catch_data` as loaded, and the output sections compute their own
landings and discard sums directly off it. Nothing in this vignette reads a
`stratum_id`.

# Manual grouping

Hand-written quosures, checked and raised with `check_group_conditions()` and
`catchRaising()` directly.

These are the same six groups as the RDBESStockCoord example this is based on
(that example calls the gear column `gear`; `derive_fields()` names the same
thing `metier4`, so the conditions here use `metier4`). G1-G3 split the main
gears, G4 is a REST group for everything else, G5 pulls out the `fleetValue`
sentinel for incidental bycatch (IBC), G6 is BMS on its own - between them
every row is claimed exactly once, discards or not.

```{r strata-cond}
strataCond_manual <- list(
  G1 = quo(metier4 == "TBB" & catchCategory != "BMS"),
  G2 = quo(metier4 %in% c("GTR", "GNS") & catchCategory != "BMS"),
  G3 = quo(metier4 %in% c("OTB", "SSC", "SDN") & catchCategory != "BMS"),
  G4 = quo(!metier4 %in% c("TBB", "GTR", "GNS", "OTB", "SSC", "SDN") &
             catchCategory != "BMS" & fleetValue != "MIS_MIS_0_0_0_IBC"),
  G5 = quo(fleetValue == "MIS_MIS_0_0_0_IBC" & catchCategory != "BMS"),
  G6 = quo(catchCategory == "BMS"))
```

`matchedDataCond`: G1-G3, G5 and G6 are raised on their own strata (the same
condition, reused). G4 (REST) has too little discard data of its own and draws
on every gear instead - minus five strata whose own discard ratio the source
example flagged as implausible (verified present in this bll 2025 data too:
Sweden / 27.3.a.21 and France / 27.7.e both occur). Remove the `!(...)` block
to see their effect on G4's rate.

```{r matched-cond}
matchedDataCond_manual <- list(
  G1 = strataCond_manual$G1,
  G2 = strataCond_manual$G2,
  G3 = strataCond_manual$G3,
  G4 = quo(catchCategory != "BMS" &
             fleetValue != "MIS_MIS_0_0_0_IBC" &
             !((vesselFlagCountry == "Sweden" & areaValue == "27.3.a.21" &
                  fleetValue == "GNS_DEF_all_0_0_all" & seasonValue %in% c(2, 3)) |
                 (vesselFlagCountry == "Sweden" & areaValue == "27.3.a.21" &
                    fleetValue == "GTR_DEF_all_0_0_all" & seasonValue %in% c(2, 4)) |
                 (vesselFlagCountry == "France" & areaValue == "27.7.e" &
                    fleetValue == "GTR_DEF_100-119_0_0_all" & seasonValue == 2) |
                 (vesselFlagCountry == "Sweden" & areaValue == "27.3.a.21" &
                    fleetValue == "OTB_CRU_90-119_0_0_all" & seasonValue == 3) |
                 (vesselFlagCountry == "Sweden" & areaValue == "27.3.a.21" &
                    fleetValue == "OTB_CRU_70-89_2_35_all" & seasonValue == 1))),
  G5 = strataCond_manual$G5,
  G6 = strataCond_manual$G6)
```

## Condition diagnostics

`check_group_conditions()` is what `catchRaising()` runs internally before it
raises anything; running it separately is the "optional, automatically run
with raising, but good practice" step of the RDBESStockCoord scripts - every
stratum is checked for both a gap (claimed by no group) and an overlap
(claimed twice) before any weight moves. The engine prints a "Condition
diagnostics" banner for each condition; it is hidden here.

```{r check, results = "hide", message = FALSE}
cond_st <- check_group_conditions(catch_data = catch_data,
                                  condition_list = strataCond_manual,
                                  domain = "domainCatchDis",
                                  originType = "WGEstimate",
                                  variableType = "WeightLive",
                                  logFile = NULL, append = TRUE)
cond_md <- check_group_conditions(catch_data = catch_data,
                                  condition_list = matchedDataCond_manual,
                                  conditionType = "matched_data",
                                  domain = "domainCatchDis",
                                  originType = "WGEstimate",
                                  variableType = "WeightLive",
                                  logFile = NULL, append = TRUE)
```

Both counts should be 0, and the column sums say how many rows each group
claims:

```{r check-result}
strata_matrix <- do.call(cbind, cond_st)
cat(sprintf("manual: %d rows in no group, %d rows in more than one (both should be 0)\n",
            sum(rowSums(strata_matrix) == 0), sum(rowSums(strata_matrix) > 1)))
colSums(strata_matrix)
```

## Raise the catch

`catchRaising()` prints its own banner per condition pair, unconditionally
(the check above, run again internally) - that noise is the engine's own
logging, hidden here as well.

```{r raise, results = "hide", message = FALSE}
raised_manual <- catchRaising(catch_data = catch_data,
                              condition_raising_st_list = strataCond_manual,
                              condition_matched_data_list = matchedDataCond_manual,
                              type = "discards",
                              originType = "WGEstimate",
                              variableType = "WeightLive",
                              logFile = file.path(tempdir(), "raising_log.txt"))
```

```{r raise-result}
cat(sprintf("manual raising: %d rows (%d imported, %d raised)\n",
            nrow(raised_manual),
            sum(raised_manual$importedOrRaised == "imported"),
            sum(raised_manual$importedOrRaised == "raised")))
```

# Overview of the raised weight

Imported against raised, at any aggregation. `plot_raised_composition()` takes
any catch-side column on `x` and an optional `facet`: landings / discards are
always the fill, imported / raised is always the shading, and whatever you put
on `x` or `facet` is the aggregation.

```{r overview-table}
raised_overview_table(raised = raised_manual)
```

By metier:

```{r overview-metier, fig.alt = "Imported and raised weight by metier"}
plot_raised_composition(raised = raised_manual, x_var = "metier4")
```

By metier, faceted by country - a finer aggregation than the group
definitions themselves ever used:

```{r overview-country, fig.height = 6.5, fig.alt = "Imported and raised weight by metier, one panel per country"}
plot_raised_composition(raised = raised_manual, x_var = "metier4", facet_var = "Country")
```

# Discard rate across the raising groups

Not how much weight moved, but whether the *strata a group draws its rate
from* agree with each other. `plot_discard_rate()` draws one point per stratum
from any table carrying a discard rate; put the raising **group** on `x` and
every point under a group is one of the strata that fed its rate - a group
with points scattered from 2% to 40% is not a group, it is a guess, no matter
how well it covers the stock.

The table is `matchedDataCond_manual` filtered straight against `catch_data`,
with each group's rows turned into one donor stratum per `domainCatchDis` +
`metier4` by `build_coverage_strata()` - the same granularity `catchRaising()`
itself estimates a ratio from, and the same check the source example runs
before raising ("Per-stratum spread behind each group average"). A stratum
table at `metier4` + `Country` + `Season` cannot stand in here: `catchCategory`
and `fleetValue` (both load-bearing above, G4's exclusions especially) do not
survive that aggregation.

The table's `rate` is discards / covered landings - the very number the CAS
output reports as `rate` (there per CEF row, here per donor stratum), so what
is plotted here is what ends up in the CAS.

```{r donors}
donor_detail_manual <- bind_rows(lapply(names(matchedDataCond_manual), function(g) {
  donors <- catch_data %>%
    filter(!!matchedDataCond_manual[[g]],
           !is.na(domainCatchDis),
           originType == "WGEstimate",
           variableType == "WeightLive") %>%
    build_coverage_strata(dims = c("domainCatchDis", "metier4"))
  # NULL for a group with no landings / discards among its donors at all
  # (G6 is BMS only; G5 has no WGEstimate discard record - see the CAS section)
  if (!is.null(donors)) mutate(donors, donor_group = g, .before = 1)
}))
```

```{r donors-plot, fig.height = 5, fig.alt = "Discard rate of the donor strata, by raising group, coloured by metier"}
plot_discard_rate(catch = donor_detail_manual, x = "donor_group", colour = "metier4",
                  jitter = TRUE)
```

```{r donors-summary}
donor_detail_manual %>% group_by(donor_group) %>%
  summarise(n = n(),
            mean_rate = round(weighted.mean(rate, w = weightingTotal, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
            sd_rate = round(sd(rate, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
            min_rate = round(min(rate, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
            max_rate = round(max(rate, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
            .groups = "drop")
```

# Output: CC (Catch Combined)

One row per `catchCategory`, the stock-wide raised total. The headline number
this vignette exists to produce: total landings and total (sampled + raised)
discards for the stock, in tonnes. One row per `catchCategory` actually
present in `raised_manual` - usually `Lan` and `Dis`, but `BMS` too if the
stock reports it; nothing below is hardcoded to just those two.

`car_version`, `car_version_desc` and `car_scheme_name` identify *this*
allocation scheme's run - a different scheme (the hierarchical one, or a
different manual rule set) would carry a different version, so several runs'
CC / CAR / CAS outputs can sit in the same downstream table without being
confused for each other. All three are reused as they are in the next
section - keep every use in sync if any of them changes.

```{r cc}
car_version      <- 1
car_version_desc <- "Manual_Stock_Annex"
car_scheme_name  <- "Stock_Annex"

# year / workingGroup / stock come straight off the loaded data, not typed in
# by hand - assumed constant across the whole run (one stock, one year); the
# stopifnot catches it loudly if that is ever not true rather than silently
# picking the first value.
year_val         <- unique(catch_data$year)
workingGroup_val <- unique(catch_data$workingGroup)
stock_val        <- unique(catch_data$stock)
stopifnot(length(year_val) == 1, length(workingGroup_val) == 1,
          length(stock_val) == 1)

cc_out <- raised_manual %>%
  filter(originType == "WGEstimate", variableType == "WeightLive") %>%
  group_by(catchCategory) %>%
  summarise(total = round(sum(total, na.rm = TRUE) / 1000, 3), .groups = "drop") %>%
  transmute(recordType = "CC", version = car_version,
            versionDescription = car_version_desc,
            calendarYear = "Y", year = year_val,
            workingGroup = workingGroup_val, stock = stock_val,
            catchCategory,
            seasonType = NA_character_, seasonValue = NA_character_,
            areaType = NA_character_, areaValue = NA_character_,
            fleetValue = NA_character_,
            variableType = "WeightLive", variableUnit = "t",
            total, variance = NA_real_, numTrips = NA_integer_)
cc_out
```

# Output: CAR and CAS (detailed)

Two tables sharing one allocation-scheme identity (`recordType`, `version`,
`versionDescription` and `catchAllocationSchemeName` line up between them, the
same values the CC section already set) - kept as two separate data frames
for now, per-row CAR and per-donor-stratum CAS. Combining them into one csv
with CAS appended under CAR, and writing either to disk, is future work.

## CAR: every row `catchRaising()` produced

Each row is tagged with the **group** that raised it. `catchAllocationGroupName`
is filled *only* where a row was actually raised (blank on every imported row -
nothing raised it, so there is nothing to name); `imported` is Y / N, matching
the source RDBESStockCoord convention rather than rcef's own "imported" /
"raised" wording. The group is rebuilt here by re-testing every row against
`strataCond_manual` - the same partition `check_group_conditions()` already
confirmed above is exhaustive and non-overlapping, so exactly one group
matches every row (imported or raised alike); only *raised* rows keep it. The
engine records the same thing in its own `DrGroup` column, which is checked
against the re-test below, so the tag does not depend on an engine column.

```{r car}
raised_manual <- raised_manual %>%
  mutate(.car_group = case_when(
    !!strataCond_manual$G1 ~ "G1",
    !!strataCond_manual$G2 ~ "G2",
    !!strataCond_manual$G3 ~ "G3",
    !!strataCond_manual$G4 ~ "G4",
    !!strataCond_manual$G5 ~ "G5",
    !!strataCond_manual$G6 ~ "G6",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_))

# the engine's own DrGroup agrees with the re-test on every raised row
with(subset(raised_manual, importedOrRaised == "raised"),
     all(DrGroup == .car_group))

car_out <- raised_manual %>%
  mutate(recordType = "CAR",
         version = car_version,
         versionDescription = car_version_desc,
         catchAllocationSchemeName = car_scheme_name,
         catchAllocationGroupName = if_else(importedOrRaised == "raised",
                                            .car_group, NA_character_),
         imported = if_else(importedOrRaised == "imported", "Y", "N")) %>%
  select(-.car_group, -importedOrRaised) %>%
  select(recordType, version, versionDescription, catchAllocationSchemeName,
         catchAllocationGroupName, imported, everything())

cat(sprintf("CAR: %d rows x %d columns (%d imported, %d raised across %d groups)\n",
            nrow(car_out), ncol(car_out),
            sum(car_out$imported == "Y"), sum(car_out$imported == "N"),
            n_distinct(car_out$catchAllocationGroupName, na.rm = TRUE)))
```

`car_out` carries the scheme identity columns first, then every column of the
raised table. The raised rows first, key columns only:

```{r car-head}
car_out %>%
  arrange(desc(imported == "N"), catchAllocationGroupName) %>%
  select(catchAllocationGroupName, imported, vesselFlagCountry, seasonValue,
         areaValue, fleetValue, catchCategory, total) %>%
  head(10)
```

## CAS: the donor strata behind each group's rate

Only the imported `Dis` rows that satisfy at least one group's
`matchedDataCond` - the ones `catchRaising()` actually pulled a rate from.
Unlike CAR, this is **not** a partition: G4's `matchedDataCond` draws on every
gear (see the manual grouping above), so a stratum that is G1's own donor is
*also* one of G4's many donors - it appears once *per group it feeds*, not once
per row.

`weightingTotal` and `rate` are per this stratum, matched on `domainCatchDis` -
the column CEF itself uses to link a `Dis` estimate to its domain:
`weightingTotal` is that domain's own landed weight (kg, same unit as `total` -
unlike the CC table, CAR and CAS stay in the CEF's native kg throughout), and
`rate` is this row's discards over that landed weight (discards / landings,
*not* the raising side's `discard_rate` = discards / (landings + discards) -
matching the source RDBESStockCoord convention's unbounded `dis_ratio`, and
the same `rate` `build_coverage_strata()` and `plot_discard_rate()` use,
confirmed against the reference CAR-CAS_detailed.csv: its `rate` column is
exactly `total / weightingTotal`, occasionally above 1).

```{r cas}
landings_by_domain <- catch_data %>%
  filter(catchCategory == "Lan", originType == "WGEstimate",
         variableType == "WeightLive", !is.na(domainCatchDis)) %>%
  group_by(domainCatchDis) %>%
  summarise(.landings = sum(total, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

cas_out <- bind_rows(lapply(names(matchedDataCond_manual), function(g)
  catch_data %>%
    filter(!!matchedDataCond_manual[[g]], catchCategory == "Dis",
           !is.na(domainCatchDis), originType == "WGEstimate",
           variableType == "WeightLive") %>%
    mutate(catchAllocationGroupName = g))) %>%
  left_join(landings_by_domain, by = "domainCatchDis") %>%
  mutate(recordType = "CAS",
         version = car_version,
         versionDescription = car_version_desc,
         catchAllocationSchemeName = car_scheme_name,
         imported = "Y",
         weightingCategory = "Lan",
         weightingParameter = "WeightLive",
         averagingMethod = "weighted",
         weightingTotal = round(.landings, 3),
         rate = round(total / .landings, 4)) %>%
  select(-.landings) %>%
  select(recordType, version, versionDescription, catchAllocationSchemeName,
         catchAllocationGroupName, imported, everything())

cat(sprintf("CAS: %d donor rows x %d columns across %d groups (%d distinct strata - some strata donate to more than one group)\n",
            nrow(cas_out), ncol(cas_out), n_distinct(cas_out$catchAllocationGroupName),
            n_distinct(cas_out$domainCatchDis)))
```

The first donor rows, key columns only:

```{r cas-head}
cas_out %>%
  arrange(catchAllocationGroupName) %>%
  select(catchAllocationGroupName, vesselFlagCountry, areaValue, fleetValue,
         domainCatchDis, total, weightingTotal, rate) %>%
  head(10)
```

## Do CAR and CAS describe the same groups?

Every group CAR raised something for should have at least one CAS donor row,
and vice versa - the two tables describing the same groups, not two different
countings. A group *can* legitimately fail this (this data's G5 / IBC does):
`catchRaising()` and every donor filter above are restricted to
`originType == "WGEstimate"`, so a group whose own discard records all carry
some *other* `originType` (IBC's here are all `"Official"`) has no
`WGEstimate` donor at all - CAS then has no row for it, and its CAR rows
raised on nothing get `total = NaN`, not a real weight. That is a genuine gap
in the **scheme** (this group cannot really be raised as defined), not a bug
in these tables - so it is printed by name below, never just a silent `FALSE`.

```{r linked}
car_groups <- na.omit(unique(car_out$catchAllocationGroupName))
cas_groups <- unique(cas_out$catchAllocationGroupName)
ok_linked <- setequal(car_groups, cas_groups)
cat(sprintf("every CAR group also appears in CAS, and vice versa: %s\n", ok_linked))
if (!ok_linked) {
  raised_no_donor  <- setdiff(car_groups, cas_groups)
  donor_not_raised <- setdiff(cas_groups, car_groups)
  if (length(raised_no_donor))
    cat(sprintf("  raised in CAR but no CAS donor (raised total is NaN - check originType): %s\n",
                paste(raised_no_donor, collapse = ", ")))
  if (length(donor_not_raised))
    cat(sprintf("  donor in CAS but nothing raised under it in CAR: %s\n",
                paste(donor_not_raised, collapse = ", ")))
}
```

`cc_out`, `car_out` and `cas_out` are plain data frames in this session;
nothing was written to a file.
